You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To improve your eyesight, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Research reputable laser eye surgery clinics (2 hours)
Step 2. Undergo initial corneal mapping (45 minutes)
Step 3. Purchase high-quality UV protection sunglasses (30 minutes)
Step 4. Apply prescribed post-operative lubricant drops (1 minute)
Step 5. Attend a general eye health seminar (3 hours)
Step 6. Practice distant object focusing exercises (15 minutes)
Step 7. Schedule a consultation with a retina specialist (10 minutes)
Step 8. Complete a contrast sensitivity test (20 minutes)
Step 9. Review patient testimonial videos (1 hour)
Step 10. Finalize the surgical plan with the lead surgeon (30 minutes)
Step 11. Book a comprehensive vision baseline exam (15 minutes)
Step 12. Evaluate the health of the optic nerve (25 minutes)
Step 13. Pay the clinic deposit (10 minutes)
Step 14. Receive a detailed pre-op instruction packet (5 minutes)
Step 15. Research the benefits of lutein supplements (40 minutes)
Step 16. Perform a dry-eye assessment (20 minutes)
Step 17. Measure the thickness of the cornea (15 minutes)
Step 18. Undergo a final pupil dilation check (30 minutes)
Step 19. Take a specialized glaucoma screening (20 minutes)
Step 20. Rest in a dark room to stabilize vision (2 hours)
Step 21. Perform 20-20-20 rule eye breaks throughout the day (8 hours)
Step 22. Sanitize all diagnostic equipment (10 minutes)
Step 23. Buy blue-light filtering screen protectors (20 minutes)
Step 24. Conduct a peripheral vision field test (30 minutes)
Step 25. Complete an online vision habit survey (15 minutes)
Step 26. Verify insurance coverage for corrective procedures (1 day)
Step 27. Update your emergency contact information (5 minutes)
Step 28. Receive a post-care kit with eye shields (10 minutes)
Step 29. Log your daily visual clarity levels (5 minutes)
Step 30. Check for signs of ocular hypertension (15 minutes)
Step 31. Practice rapid refocusing drills (10 minutes)
Step 32. Consult with a nutritionist regarding Vitamin A (1 hour)
Step 33. Set up a dim lighting environment for recovery (30 minutes)
Step 34. Download a vision tracking mobile app (5 minutes)
Step 35. Watch a tutorial on proper eye drop administration (10 minutes)
Step 36. Perform near-point convergence exercises (15 minutes)
Step 37. List all current medications for the doctor (20 minutes)
Step 38. Get a referral for a secondary opinion (5 minutes)
Step 39. Evaluate night vision capabilities (40 minutes)
Step 40. Wash your face with hypoallergenic soap (5 minutes)
Step 41. Purchase a one-month supply of omega-3 fatty acids (15 minutes)
Step 42. Order custom-fit protective goggles (20 minutes)
Step 43. Clean all household fans to reduce dust (1 hour)
Step 44. Take a non-prescription anti-inflammatory (5 minutes)
Step 45. Read about the history of refractive surgery (2 hours)
Step 46. Undergo a tear film stability test (15 minutes)
Step 47. Remove all eye makeup and debris (10 minutes)
Step 48. Organize a ride home for the day of the procedure (30 minutes)
Step 49. Sign the informed consent forms (15 minutes)
Step 50. Abstain from wearing contact lenses (1 week)
Step 51. Avoid swimming in chlorinated pools (3 days)
Step 52. Confirm the date and time of the operation (5 minutes)
Step 53. Buy a wide-brimmed hat for outdoor use (20 minutes)
Step 54. Receive the local anesthetic numbing drops (10 minutes)
Step 55. Arrive at the surgical center (30 minutes)
Step 56. Discuss family history of cataracts (30 minutes)
Step 57. Receive the final "all-clear" for the procedure (5 minutes)
Step 58. Rest your eyes for a full night's sleep (8 hours)
Step 59. Use a warm compress on the eyelids (15 minutes)
Step 60. Install a flicker-free monitor (30 minutes)
Step 61. Administer the primary corrective laser treatment (15 minutes)
Step 62. Prepare a list of questions for the surgeon (20 minutes)
Step 63. Attend a pre-assessment counseling session (1 hour)
Step 64. Take a high-dose Vitamin C supplement (2 minutes)
Step 65. Set up an ergonomic workstation (1 hour)
Step 66. Practice blinking consciously while using screens (1 hour)
Step 67. Perform an automated refraction test (10 minutes)
Step 68. Attend a mandatory safety briefing (45 minutes)
Step 69. Apply a protective bandage lens (5 minutes)
Step 70. Undergo a physical health screening (1 hour)
Step 71. Spend time in a green, natural environment (2 hours)
Step 72. Measure intraocular pressure (10 minutes)
Step 73. Buy a new bottle of sterile saline solution (10 minutes)
Step 74. Review the surgery day checklist (15 minutes)
Step 75. Discuss potential side effects with a nurse (30 minutes)
Step 76. Purchase a magnifying glass for temporary use (15 minutes)
Step 77. Avoid rubbing your eyes for any reason (12 hours)
Step 78. Listen to an audiobook to avoid screen strain (2 hours)
Step 79. Undergo a color blindness assessment (15 minutes)
Step 80. Limit caffeine intake to reduce eye twitching (1 day)
Step 81. Perform a manual "puff" air test (5 minutes)
Step 82. Clean your current glasses with microfiber (5 minutes)
Step 83. Check the alignment of the visual axis (20 minutes)
Step 84. Review the surgeon's credentials (1 hour)
Step 85. Measure the diameter of your pupils in low light (10 minutes)
Step 86. Take a prescribed mild sedative (30 minutes)
Step 87. Fast for the required period before the procedure (6 hours)
Step 88. Set an alarm for your medication schedule (5 minutes)
Step 89. Receive a prescription for antibiotic drops (10 minutes)
Step 90. Take a digital photograph of the retina (5 minutes)
Step 91. Dispose of old, expired eye drops (5 minutes)
Step 92. Calibrate the laser equipment (30 minutes)
Step 93. Sit in the waiting room for the post-op check (20 minutes)
Step 94. Allow the flap to heal naturally (2 days)
Step 95. Perform a follow-up visual acuity test (20 minutes)
Step 96. Research different types of intraocular lenses (2 hours)
Step 97. Adjust the brightness on all digital devices (10 minutes)
Step 98. Take a nap to facilitate cellular repair (2 hours)
Step 99. Purchase preservative-free artificial tears (15 minutes)
Step 100. Review the long-term maintenance plan (30 minutes)
